I farm only 9 mu, so I will keep the plan simple and steady. I have 30 years in the field, and with well irrigation I trust wheat-maize as my main line because it is the surest way for me to keep grain in hand and use the land fully. I will put 6 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and leave 3 mu for cotton, because cotton gives me cash income but I do not want too much of it since it needs more pest control and more careful field work. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few times, and aim for a stable yield rather than chasing the very highest output. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 6 mu because hybrid maize performs better for me and matches the summer season well. I will feed maize a bit more nitrogen than wheat and water it a couple of times if rainfall is not enough. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area, use improved seed, fertilize it in a balanced way, irrigate several times from the well, and spray more often than the grain crops because insects are usually the bigger problem there. I will use rotary tillage on all fields because it saves labor, fits my scale, and is what I can manage reliably with my conditions.
